history.text: Supplier review completed with the export team in Korea. Standard ordering arrangements and monthly sailing schedules remain unchanged.
Both lines arrived within the agreed delivery window. Invoice prices matched the purchase order and the receipt was booked as normal.
The quarterly sales review recorded steady demand for this line. The existing ordering cadence remains appropriate.
The supplier confirmed its current export price list continues to apply to our UK orders. Payment terms and minimum order quantities are unchanged.
The latest consignment was delivered on the agreed date. Carton quantities and packing details matched the purchase order.
Routine range review completed. Sales remained consistent with the normal ordering pattern for both lines.
Monthly purchasing call completed. Recent deliveries have followed the agreed schedule, and the supplier confirmed that prices and standard trading terms remain unchanged.
The supplier confirmed that export orders are consolidated at its Busan warehouse before shipment to the UK. Purchasing requested advance notice of any changes to the agreed dispatch schedule.
The revised samples passed our dimensional and finish checks. The supplier was authorised to use the approved packaging specifications for subsequent orders.
The supplier reported significant dispatch delays following industrial action at its packing contractor. Completed orders remain awaiting packing, and no revised departure dates have been confirmed.
The supplier advised that the packing backlog remains unresolved for both lines. Purchasing requested separate dispatches where cartons can be released without waiting for the rest of the order.
Purchasing issued an alternative sourcing brief covering dimensions, materials and retail packaging for both products. Any proposed substitute must pass sample approval before an order is placed.

The supplier confirmed that packing has resumed, but an ongoing backlog is still delaying export dispatches. Purchasing requested a confirmed carton release list and written booking confirmation from the forwarder.
Completed the annual supplier review. The supplier confirmed that UK export orders continue to be consolidated at its Busan warehouse before shipment.

Approved the revised outer carton artwork following confirmation that the UK importer address and cooking instructions were correct. The supplier will use the revised cartons for orders packed from November.

The supplier advised that lead times for all products will increase by four weeks, from eight to twelve weeks, for purchase orders placed from 23 February. It attributed the extension to reduced packing capacity during a production-line refurbishment.

Purchasing confirmed that the additional four weeks applies to all three products, with no exceptions currently available. Existing accepted orders retain their previously confirmed dispatch dates; future orders will be planned against the twelve-week lead time.
Supplier review: Ulsan Leaf & Beverage Co. confirmed that UK orders will continue to be consolidated at its Busan forwarder. Purchase orders must show the agreed English carton descriptions.
A UK grocery chain confirmed a listing for YujaHoneySpark in 48 shops from January 2026. Its opening order is separate from the proposed weekly replenishment schedule.

The grocery chain's first three weekly sales reports show YujaHoneySpark selling 28% above its launch forecast. The buyer has requested that we use the revised forecast for February replenishment planning.

Purchasing sent the supplier an updated YujaHoneySpark order forecast reflecting the UK retailer's stronger sales. The supplier acknowledged receipt and asked for firm quantities before reserving the next production slot.

The UK online retailer confirmed that its winter promotion for PearGingerInfusion ended on 15 February. It has reduced its March order forecast by 20% against February and does not plan to extend the promotional price.
Supplier approval review completed for the Korean milling and blending site. Requested current sieve inspection records and evidence of corrective actions from the previous hygiene audit.
Two UK customers reported small blue plastic fragments in separate production lots. Sent photographs and retained sample references to the supplier and requested a documented investigation.

The supplier traced the fragments to worn plastic scrapers used on shared blending equipment. It reported replacing the scrapers and introducing pre-start equipment checks across all flour and baking mix lines.

Further customer complaints described blue fragments in both products. Asked the supplier to reconcile these lot dates with its scraper replacement records and provide evidence that the earlier corrective action had been verified.

An independent site audit found incomplete equipment inspection sheets and no recorded effectiveness checks for the foreign-body corrective action. Purchasing placed new orders on hold pending an agreed corrective action plan and technical approval.

Received a corrective action plan covering replacement of plastic contact parts, revised sieve checks and operator retraining. Technical requested dated maintenance evidence and completed inspection records rather than blank templates.

The follow-up review found that maintenance evidence had been supplied, but inspection records remained incomplete on two blending shifts. Purchasing confirmed that the order hold would remain until technical signed off the outstanding audit findings.
Supplier review completed with the export team in Busan. Purchase orders for UK shipments require written confirmation of production slots before freight is booked.

The supplier reported a sharp increase in Korean orders following a domestic television feature on RoastedSesameKnifeNoodles. Its Korean retail customers have requested additional production for October; our export allocation has not yet been confirmed.

The supplier confirmed that additional Korean supermarket orders have taken the next available noodle production slots. The quoted order-to-dispatch lead time for RoastedSesameKnifeNoodles has increased from four to seven weeks.
The export manager confirmed that ChestnutFiveGrainRice runs on a separate production line. Its agreed dispatch date remains unchanged despite the additional domestic noodle orders.

The supplier offered a split dispatch for our noodle order, with the first portion leaving on the original date and the balance three weeks later. Purchasing requested carton quantities and revised freight costs before accepting.

The supplier advised that Korean repeat orders remain above its pre-promotion forecast. Export noodle orders are still being allocated by confirmed production slot, and the supplier requested an eight-week forward order schedule from us.
Annual supplier review completed. The supplier confirmed that export orders will continue to be consolidated at Busan, with packing lists issued before collection.
Approved the revised outer cartons following a handling trial. The supplier will retain the existing pack quantities and add clearer batch references.
Purchasing requested updated fragrance declarations for the next order cycle. Any proposed formulation change must be reviewed before an order is placed.
The supplier reported a sharp increase in orders for CitrusSinkFoam over the previous fortnight. It asked customers to submit firm purchase orders earlier so that production slots could be allocated.

The supplier confirmed that demand remains above its original production plan. Purchasing requested a confirmed dispatch date for the next order and asked whether an additional production run could be arranged.
Annual supplier review completed with the export team in Korea. Factory contact details and the bank account verification record were confirmed unchanged.

Approved the revised English-language label proofs following checks of ingredients, allergen emphasis and UK importer details. The supplier confirmed that the approved artwork would be used for the next production run.
The commercial invoice showed the previous carton price rather than the agreed purchase order price. A corrected invoice was received on 24 July and passed to accounts before payment.

Warehouse receiving instructions were updated to include photographs of jar seals and outer carton damage. Buyers will attach the instructions to future purchase orders for these products regardless of supplier.

The October shipment departed Busan three days later than booked following a vessel schedule change. The forwarder arranged an earlier UK delivery slot after clearance, and the customer orders linked to the shipment were dispatched by their agreed dates.
Routine sample checks found the texture, colour and pack seals consistent with the approved reference samples. Results were filed against the relevant production batches.
The supplier sent its spring production calendar and confirmed the purchase order cut-off dates for April departures. Purchasing circulated the dates to the sales and logistics teams.
The purchasing team received the revised export price list and carton specifications from the Busan office. Prices are quoted in US dollars, with freight booked separately.

There have been reports of loose closures and damaged outer cartons, although the summary does not identify the affected lines or the source of the reports. We have requested photographs and batch references before agreeing any corrective action.
Goods-in inspection recorded scuff marks on three samples from the August receipt. The purchasing team asked the warehouse to retain the samples and photograph the internal packing.
The supplier submitted revised English care instructions for approval. We requested that the dishwasher guidance be supported by the relevant test report before the artwork is released.

There have been reports of packing inconsistencies and delayed paperwork, but the meeting notes do not establish whether these relate to the supplier generally or to particular products. Purchasing has asked for the original correspondence and shipment references.
Annual supplier review completed for the Korean health foods range. Updated product specifications and UK label artwork were requested for approval before any packaging changes.

Goods-in inspection found that batch BSP251014 carried an English label which omitted milk from the ingredients and allergen declaration, although the approved specification includes milk powder. The batch was quarantined and purchasing instructed the supplier to suspend further dispatches of this product.

Traceability checks confirmed that no units from batch BSP251014 had been released to customers. QA notified the local authority food safety officer and requested the supplier's packing records, label reconciliation and investigation report.

The supplier's investigation identified use of an obsolete English label file at its contract packing site. The supplier agreed to fund disposal of the affected batch and introduce documented artwork version checks and line-clearance sign-off.

The quarantined batch was destroyed by the appointed waste contractor, and the destruction certificate was filed. QA approved corrected UK artwork showing milk in the ingredients list with the required emphasis; this approval did not authorise dispatch.

The supplier's credit note for the destroyed batch has been received. Evidence of staff training and a completed label reconciliation from the next production run remain outstanding, so the dispatch hold remains in place pending QA review.
Annual supplier details checked against the purchasing records. The Korean production address, export contact and payment details remain unchanged.
Reviewed the latest specifications and UK label proofs for both products. Ingredient declarations and allergen wording match the approved files; no amendments requested.

Supplier advised that production scheduling around the Lunar New Year will extend lead times by four weeks for orders placed during February. Purchasing has noted the revised timing for the next order cycle.
The supplier confirmed that UK orders will be handled by its export team in Busan. Purchase orders should quote the agreed sterling price list and request shipment by refrigerated container.
Approved the revised outer carton artwork after the supplier added the UK importer address. The retail pack recipe and declared allergens remain unchanged.
Warehouse intake staff have been asked to photograph date codes on the first pallet of each delivery. These photographs will be retained with the goods receipt records for traceability.
The supplier advised that its export office will close from 6 to 8 October for Chuseok. Orders requiring confirmation before the closure should be submitted by 26 September.
The supplier proposed a stronger tray seal following two damaged sample packs. Replacement samples passed our handling checks, and the revised seal was approved for the next production run.
Received updated product specifications and cooking instructions. Technical review found no changes to ingredients or allergens; the documents have been filed against the product records.

Agreed to consolidate the next purchase orders into one frozen shipment, with each order shown separately on the packing list. The supplier will send draft shipping documents for approval before dispatch.
Completed the annual review of retail case quantities and barcode records. No amendments were required, and the existing details have been retained in the purchasing system.
